X.finding: Claim email concatenated into the system prompt (prompt injection)
X.why: TriageService.java:36-41 appends email to the instruction text and :51 sends it via .system(prompt); the report gives the attacker payload (APPROVE, amount 50000) and links it to payment.

X.finding: Full prompt (claim email) and answer logged at INFO; e.getMessage() logged

X.finding: Content read without checking stopReason (refusal / max_tokens)
X.why: TriageService.java:55 reads content().get(0).text().get() with no stopReason() check; the report names refusal and max_tokens truncation and that both are retried.

X.finding: Client built per attempt and 5-attempt loop wrapping SDK retries
X.why: TriageService.java:46 builds a new AnthropicOkHttpClient each attempt and never closes it; :44 loops 5 times around the SDK's own retries. Both halves are named.

X.finding: Unbounded, unvalidated claim email and no rate limit
X.why: ClaimsController.java:18 ClaimRequest(String email) has no @NotBlank/@Size and :28 has no @Valid; validation starter is in pom.xml:19. The report says a 5 MB email goes to the paid API.
TriageResult.java:4 amountClaimed is double and PaymentService.java:16,20 take double amount; the report gives the rounding example.

X.finding: Repeated POST for the same claimId pays twice (no idempotency)
X.why: ClaimsController.java:27-31 re-runs triage on every POST and TriageService.java:66-67 pays each time; nothing records that the claim was already paid, so a client retry creates a second payment instruction.

X.finding: catch (Exception) treats every failure alike and retries it
X.why: TriageService.java:58 catches all exceptions, so a 400, a refusal or a JSON parse error is retried the same way as a network failure.

X.finding: Final failure surfaces as a generic 500 instead of 503 with Retry-After
X.why: TriageService.java:62-63 throws IllegalStateException, which nothing maps, so an upstream outage reaches the caller as a 500.

X.finding: Javadoc 'acts on its recommendation' shows mixed responsibilities
X.why: TriageService.java:13 Javadoc; a design opinion about splitting responsibilities, and the real harm is already K2.

X.finding: Controller holds the results Map; move it to a store class
X.why: ClaimsController.java:21 ConcurrentHashMap result storage is on the key's 'Not defects' list (demo storage).
